pattern: Cardinal base → fractional noun (-th or suppletive)

entry.name: Fractional Noun
entry.pattern: Cardinal base → fractional noun (-th or suppletive)

dimensions.form: Cardinal base + -th or suppletive (half, quarter); count noun
dimensions.meaning: Denotes denominator in fraction; partitive semantics
dimensions.function: Heads nominal in fraction NPs; numerator is determiner
dimensions.distribution: Inflects for number (one fifth, two fifths); licenses factors

1.definition: Fractional noun denoting a denominator; used in fraction NPs with a numeral determiner

constraints.description: Fractional noun heads a nominal; numerator functions as determiner in fraction NPs (e.g., one fifth).
Fractional noun inflects for number (one third vs two thirds); half/quarter are suppletive.

projection.target: Fifths in three fifths accepts plural marking and a cardinal determiner. Fifth in fifth place is adjectival and does not take plural marking there. The two distributions persist where the forms are partly identical.
projection.evidence: CGEL and Reynolds distinguish fractional nouns from ordinal adjectives despite the shared morphological material.

curious.title: Fraction words as nouns
curious.summary: In a fraction like one fifth, the word fifth names the size of the pieces and behaves like a noun.
curious.body:
In one fifth, the word fifth names the size of the pieces, and the number in front counts them. Because it's a noun, it takes a plural ending when there's more than one: one third, but two thirds.

Some fraction words are made by adding -th to a number word, as in fifth. Others, such as half and quarter, are separate words that aren't built that way. This dictionary treats fifth in a fraction as different from fifth in fifth place, where it describes a position and takes no plural, even though the two look the same.
curious.try: Say one fifth, then two fifths. What happens to the end of the word? Does fifth place change the same way?

teacher.summary: Separates fraction nouns (three fifths) from ordinal adjectives (fifth place), which share morphological material.
teacher.explain: A fractional noun denotes a denominator and heads the nominal in a fraction NP, with the numerator in determiner function (one fifth). It's a count noun and inflects for number: one third, two thirds. Half and quarter are suppletive, not formed with -th. The same form can be an ordinal adjective in another use: fifth in fifth place is adjectival and takes no plural, while fifths in three fifths takes plural marking and a cardinal determiner. This dictionary, which is provisional, treats these as separate categories despite the shared form.
teacher.terms: Fraction word, with numerator and denominator, are the traditional terms. Ordinal number is the traditional name for what this dictionary calls an ordinal adjective.

contrasts.note: Fractional noun, plural, with a cardinal determiner.

watch_for: A learner might add plural marking to fifth in fifth place, as if it were the fraction noun.
A learner might expect half and quarter to be formed with -th like fifth.
teacher.activity: Give students a pie drawn in fifths. They shade one, two and three pieces and write the fraction in words each time, then write a sentence using fifth to give a position in a race and compare the two uses.

child.hook: What happens to the word third when you have two pieces?
child.explain: A fraction word names the size of the pieces. One third has one piece. With two pieces you say two thirds, adding an s. Half and quarter are special words.

examples.text: I coloured [two thirds] of the picture.
She ate [one quarter] of the pizza.

child.play: Say one third, then two thirds. Now try one fifth and two fifths. Which part of the word changes when there's more than one piece?
